description: Finding 5 (Medium) - Session cookie resurrection. A stale session cookie from a deleted-then-recreated username re-authenticates as the new principal because add_user creates records with no session_epoch (defaults to 0) and delete_user neither bumps the epoch nor leaves a tombstone. Fix: give new users a non-resettable epoch, and on delete bump+persist a tombstone so a recreate cannot reset the epoch below the deleted account's last value. Independent of FEAT-002/003/004 (touches _user_session_epoch in app.py and add_user/delete_user in admin.py).
steps: In identity_provider_server/app.py, add a helper (closure within create_app, near _user_session_epoch ~line 2018) `_load_deleted_epochs()` that reads `data / 'deleted_epochs.json'` (the create_app `data` Path) and returns a dict username->int, returning {} on missing file or JSONDecodeError (catch OSError/json.JSONDecodeError only).
Modify `_user_session_epoch` (app.py ~2018) to return `max(int(user.get('session_epoch', 0)), int(_load_deleted_epochs().get(username, 0)))`, preserving the existing TypeError/ValueError guard.
In identity_provider_server/admin.py `add_user` (~line 1200), add `"session_epoch": int(time.time())` to the new_user dict (time is already imported) so a recreated username never starts at 0.

In identity_provider_server/admin.py add a helper `_write_deleted_epoch(target: str, epoch: int) -> None` that, when `data_dir is not None`, reads `data_dir / 'deleted_epochs.json'` (merge existing, {} on missing/corrupt), sets `mapping[target] = max(mapping.get(target, 0), epoch)`, and writes it back as JSON with mode 0600 (use os.open with 0o600 or chmod after write, following the save_users_fn / audit 0600 pattern). Add `import os` if not present.

In identity_provider_server/admin.py `delete_user` (~line 1221), BEFORE `del users[target]`: call `_bump_session_epoch(target)` then `_write_deleted_epoch(target, int(users[target].get('session_epoch', 0)))`. Keep the existing save_users_fn call and audit. Do NOT touch any backup/restore code.

Add tests in a new tests/test_security_remediation_20261006.py (follow the _app helper style from tests/test_security_remediation_20261003.py: copy data/idp.crt+idp.key, write users.json, set secret_key=GOOD_SECRET, secure_cookies=False, trust_proxy=False): (a) assert add_user yields a record with session_epoch > 0; (b) create user, mint a session cookie, delete the user (writes deleted_epochs.json), recreate the same username via add_user, and assert a cookie minted at epoch 0 for that username is rejected by the session verifier; (c) a @pytest.mark.smoke test for the delete-then-recreate happy path.
acceptance_criteria: Running `source /Users/topazb/python/py314/bin/activate && python -m pytest tests/test_security_remediation_20261006.py tests/test_admin_full.py tests/test_security_remediation_20261003.py -q` from the worktree passes.
add_user writes a non-zero session_epoch; delete_user writes/updates data/deleted_epochs.json; _user_session_epoch returns the max of the record epoch and the tombstone.
A session cookie minted with epoch 0 for a deleted-then-recreated username is rejected.
ruff check identity_provider_server/ is clean and bandit -r identity_provider_server/ -q reports 0 medium/high.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. Code changes:
- identity_provider_server/app.py: added closure `_load_deleted_epochs()` (immediately before `_user_session_epoch`, now ~line 2022) that reads `data / 'deleted_epochs.json'` and returns dict[str,int], catching only (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) and returning {} otherwise. `_user_session_epoch` (now ~line 2042) returns max(record_epoch, tombstone_epoch); each parse is guarded by its own try/except (TypeError, ValueError)->0. No new imports needed (json/os/Path already imported in app.py).
- identity_provider_server/admin.py: added `import os` to stdlib import block. Added closure `_write_deleted_epoch(target: str, epoch: int) -> None` right after `_bump_session_epoch` (~line 650): no-ops when data_dir is None (marked `# pragma: no cover` for the prod-always-passes-data_dir branch), reads+merges `data_dir / 'deleted_epochs.json'` ({} on OSError/JSONDecodeError), sets mapping[target]=max(existing, epoch), writes via os.open(path, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0o600) + os.fdopen. add_user new_user dict now includes `"session_epoch": int(time.time())`. delete_user, BEFORE `del users[target]`, calls `_bump_session_epoch(target)` then `_write_deleted_epoch(target, int(users[target].get('session_epoch', 0)))`. No backup/restore code touched.

deleted_epochs.json CONTRACT: lives at <data_dir>/deleted_epochs.json, mode 0600, JSON object mapping username (str) -> last session epoch (int). Monotonic per key (max). Absent file / corrupt JSON / non-int value all treated as epoch 0 (fail-open to record epoch, never crashes). NOTE: file is NOT gitignored currently and will be created at runtime in the data dir; it contains only usernames+epoch ints (no secrets). Downstream findings should add it to .gitignore if they touch .gitignore (left untouched here to stay in scope).

TIMING NOTE for later steps/tests: because delete bumps the old epoch (session_epoch was int(time.time()) at create, so tombstone = create_time+1), a recreated username's fresh record epoch (new int(time.time())) can legitimately be 1 second BELOW the tombstone. That is intentional and is exactly why the tombstone floor exists; do not assert record_epoch >= tombstone.

NEW TEST FILE: tests/test_security_remediation_20261006.py (5 tests, all green). Helpers `_admin_app`/`_admin_client`/`_tokens`/`_post`/`_add_user`/`_delete_user` drive the real /admin panel. Tests: test_add_user_sets_nonzero_session_epoch; test_delete_writes_tombstone_and_rejects_resurrected_cookie (asserts epoch-0 cookie for recreated user yields no SAMLResponse on /aws); test_tombstone_floor_only_grows; test_corrupt_tombstone_value_is_ignored (covers app.py TypeError/ValueError tombstone guard, lines were 2055-2056); test_delete_then_recreate_happy_path (@pytest.mark.smoke).

VERIFICATION (all pass): targeted trio green (119 passed); ruff clean; bandit 0 medium/0 high (13 pre-existing Low only); `pytest -m smoke` 28 passed incl. the coverage gate; full in-process suite 653 passed at 100% coverage (app.py and admin.py both 100%). CHANGELOG.md Unreleased gained a 'Security (code review idp-2026-10-06)' subsection for F5. Committed on branch security/20261006-f2-f5-medium.
